title: TVS Motor Profit Jumps 51% to Record Rs 1,174 Crore as Premium Bike Demand Defies Rising Costs
excerpt: India's third-largest two-wheeler maker posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 13,896 crore, with electric vehicle sales surging 86% and total volumes crossing 1.63 million units.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • TVS Motor's Q1 FY27 profit surged 51% to Rs 1,174 crore, marking a record high.
  • Standalone revenue reached Rs 13,896 crore, a 38% increase driven by 1.63 million unit sales.
  • Electric vehicle sales jumped 86% to nearly 130,000 units, with over 1 million EV customers.
  • Commodity costs rose 45% due to global price increases amid the Iran conflict.
  • TVS shares rose 5.56% post-results, reflecting strong investor confidence.

  • TVS Motor standalone net profit rose 51% year-on-year to Rs 1,174 crore in Q1 FY27, while consolidated profit jumped 65% to Rs 1,058 crore
  • Revenue hit a record Rs 13,896 crore on a standalone basis, up 38%, driven by the highest-ever quarterly sales of 1.63 million units
  • Electric vehicle sales surged 86% to nearly 130,000 units, with TVS crossing 1 million cumulative EV customers
  • The company flagged commodity cost pressures from the Iran war and signaled a price hike in Q2 to protect margins

TVS Motor Company, India's third-largest two-wheeler manufacturer, delivered a blowout first quarter for fiscal year 2027, with profit surging past Rs 1,000 crore for the first time on the back of record sales volumes and strong demand for premium motorcycles.

The Chennai-based automaker reported standalone net profit of Rs 1,174 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, a 51% jump from Rs 776 crore a year earlier, according to filings with the stock exchanges. On a consolidated basis, profit rose 65% to Rs 1,058 crore from Rs 643 crore.

Record Revenue on Surging Volumes

Standalone revenue reached Rs 13,896 crore, a 38% increase and the company's highest-ever quarterly figure. Consolidated revenue climbed 33% to Rs 16,296 crore. The growth was fueled by record overall sales of 1.63 million two- and three-wheeler units, up 28% from the same period last year.

Premium motorcycles drove much of the margin expansion. According to Reuters, robust demand for higher-margin bikes helped cushion the blow from raw material costs that have spiked in the wake of the Iran conflict. The company's scooter brand Jupiter and its expanding electric lineup also contributed to the top-line surge.

Electric Vehicle Push Accelerates

TVS Motor's electric scooter division posted particularly strong numbers, with EV sales jumping 86% to 129,940 units. The company said it has now crossed the milestone of 1 million cumulative electric vehicle customers, solidifying its position among legacy automakers competing with EV-first startups.

Three-wheeler sales also grew 48% to 66,697 units, while the international business expanded 33% to 0.47 million units, indicating broad-based demand across segments and geographies.

Commodity Costs and the Iran War Effect

The quarter was not without headwinds. Cost of materials consumed rose 45% year-on-year as global commodity prices climbed sharply amid the ongoing Iran conflict and broader geopolitical uncertainty.

"Commodity prices witnessed a sharp upward trend during the quarter due to global market uncertainties resulting in increased input costs. The company partially mitigated the cost increases through price adjustments and focused cost optimisation initiatives, including scale benefits."

— TVS Motor Company, exchange filing

The company signaled that a price hike is likely in Q2 to offset the input cost pressure, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

Investor Reaction and Outlook

Markets responded enthusiastically to the results. TVS Motor shares surged 5.56% on the NSE, trading at Rs 3,789.90 at close. The stock's rally reflects investor confidence in the company's ability to sustain premium-led growth even as broader two-wheeler demand faces cyclical headwinds.

The company's board also approved raising up to Rs 1,000 crore through non-convertible debentures, commercial papers, or other borrowings, signaling further investment in capacity and technology.

During the quarter, TVS Motor made strategic investments of Rs 613 crore in its Singapore subsidiary and Rs 193 crore in Jana Small Finance Bank, pointing to an expansion strategy that extends beyond its core two-wheeler business.

What to Watch

The key question going forward is whether TVS Motor can maintain its margin trajectory as commodity costs remain elevated. The planned Q2 price hike will test whether consumer demand for premium two-wheelers holds firm. Investors will also watch the pace of EV adoption as government incentives evolve and competition from Ather Energy and Ola Electric intensifies.
